summary: This bill requires that any unspent federal agency appropriations be split so 49% carries over for one extra year, 49% pays down the national debt, and 2% funds capped retention bonuses for employees, while freezing the agency's next budget request at the prior level adjusted only for inflation.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a mechanism where unexpended agency appropriations are partially redirected to debt service (49%) and only a small fraction retained for bonuses, while also capping future budget requests at CPI-adjusted levels. This directly incentivizes and enforces reduced federal spending rather than allowing agencies to spend full appropriations.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or changes to the tax code.
No provisions address healthcare funding, coverage, regulation, or delivery systems.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration policy, border security, visas, or related enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or funding for related services.

The bill applies broadly to all executive agencies (including the Department of Defense) by limiting unspent appropriations and future budget growth, but it is not targeted at defense spending specifically and therefore has only incidental effects.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or related agency funding.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
No provisions address education funding, school choice, or federal involvement in schooling.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related regulations.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization policies.
The bill explicitly directs 49% of unexpended appropriations (plus any remaining bonus funds) to payments of principal and interest on the public debt, directly prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid, or related funding.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination policy.

The bill's core mechanism requires 49% of unexpended agency appropriations to be used for principal and interest payments on the public debt, with an additional 2% potentially redirected there after bonuses; it also caps future agency budget requests at CPI-adjusted levels when savings occur. This directly and centrally targets deficit reduction by converting unspent funds into debt paydown and restraining spending growth.
